judgment.rationale: The new recovery observation adds a z-order/repaint alternative to elevation. Run elevated/non-elevated and always-on-top on/off as separate axes; do not blame missing hooks alone or conflate an ordinary elevated window with the UAC secure desktop.
evidence: PowerToys0.102.3001; activate CursorHide, open Task Manager elevated, then move the pointer over it: the pointer reportedly stays invisible.
The supplied archive contains AutoHideCursor settings with hide_on_typing=true and hide_on_idle=false; the module-specific log entries do not identify a restore error.
The inspected implementation replaces system cursors and reloads them via SPI_SETCURSORS; RefreshCurrentCursor sends WM_NCHITTEST/WM_SETCURSOR to the window under the pointer.
The worker also polls cursor position on its timer, so a missing elevated hook callback alone is not a proven explanation.
The October31 follow-up suggests Task Manager always-on-top rather than elevation may determine the failure; minimizing then restoring reportedly leaves the cursor visible.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the cursor visibility, elevation, z-order and minimize/restore matrix before choosing the restore or repaint boundary.

title: CursorHide: no mouse cursor with elevated apps

actions.label: Reproduce cursor restoration and z-order matrix

setup: Use the reported hide-on-typing configuration; vary elevation and Task Manager always-on-top independently.
prerequisites: Disposable interactive Windows desktop; preserve cursor scheme and PowerToys settings; permission to open Task Manager elevated.
steps: 1. Test non-elevated Task Manager with always-on-top off, then on: hide by typing, move over the window and observe cursor restoration.
2. Repeat both cases elevated with PowerToys at standard integrity.
3. In each failing case minimize and restore Task Manager, recording whether visibility recovers and stays recovered.
4. Capture restore/refresh API return and error values with a maintainer diagnostic build; test UAC secure desktop separately, not as another normal window.
reproduce.expected_result: Movement restores the original cursor across the four ordinary-window combinations; failures and minimize recovery identify an actual restore/repaint boundary without assuming elevation is the cause.
reproduce.title: Separate CursorHide elevation and always-on-top behavior
